candidates.proposition: Release maturity and semantic authority are separate evidence dimensions.
candidates.falsification: The repaired corpus removes the prior stable-2/5 versus Beta-5/5 contrast: Pyrefly default, ty, Pyright, and mypy are all 5/5 on the frozen five-mutant corpus.
candidates.reason: Still conceptually valid, but no longer the strongest decision-changing proposition supported by this experiment.

candidates.proposition: Pyrefly has lower semantic coverage than the other tested Python type checkers.
candidates.falsification: The same Pyrefly 1.2.0 changes from 2/5 under basic to 5/5 under default on the same frozen corpus.
candidates.reason: The prior difference was configuration-sensitive and cannot be attributed to the product as a whole.

candidates.proposition: A type-checker blocking authority is the versioned execution contract, including preset/configuration, not the binary name alone.
candidates.falsification: This would fail if basic and default produced the same frozen-corpus outcome, or if the old 2/5 result remained after configuration was held constant.
candidates.reason: Same runner, same version, same five root faults, and clean baselines produced 2/5 under basic and 5/5 under default; official Pyrefly docs explicitly define different diagnostic surfaces for those presets.

candidates.proposition: After correctness gating, the fastest surviving checker should become default authority.
candidates.falsification: The protocol requires diagnostic quality, migration cost, maturity, and real-repo operational evidence in addition to timing; speed alone is not sufficient.
candidates.reason: Speed-only stories violate the preregistered editorial gate and do not resolve configuration authority.
